summary: Client retry race and service-worker replay silence final paragraph on SSE resume
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that long-running SSE streams (chat responses with lists/bulleted conclusions) sometimes arrive with the final paragraph missing after a brief network hiccup. Client uses our JS SDK behind a Chromium-based electron app with a service worker that implements a fetch handler to buffer/resume requests.

Impact:
- Occurs intermittently (estimated ~4% of sessions during heavy egress) for BlueWave Health's private deployment.
- Final paragraph or last bullet list sometimes absent — downstream UI shows a completed stream but content stops abruptly.
- Customer workflow relies on complete clinical-summary paragraphs; missing tails are high-impact.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC) in us-east-1, API fronted by customer-managed proxy + our api-gateway.
- Client: electron 20+ with service worker registration and custom fetch replays.
- Models: rw-instruct-7b (primary), fallback rw-compat-16k.

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1) Start streaming completion (SSE) for prompt that returns 3-4 paragraph summary with trailing bullet list.
2) After ~18-45s, client triggers an optimistic retry due to internal socket timeout (client-side) while service worker is attempting to replay an earlier fetch.
3) SDK reopens/resumes SSE connection and server sends resume frames.
4) Playback shows duplicated prefix fragments but the terminal paragraph/bullets are missing on the final stitched output.

Observed behavior:
- Stream resumes and finalization marker is sent by our runtime (logs show terminal event emitted).
- Client-visible assembled stream lacks the last paragraph; server-side emitted tokens appear in logs but are not present in reconstructed SSE delivered to app when the service worker replay path is used.

Expected behavior:
- Resumed SSE should deliver entire token stream including terminal paragraph and finalization metadata regardless of client-side optimistic retry or service worker replay.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Disable the service worker fetch-replay for long-poll/SSE endpoints (workaround reduces occurrence to ~0%).
- Increase client-side socket timeout to avoid optimistic retry during transient jitter.

Logs sample (server):
- runtime-session-id=rs-9a7f4e: terminal_event_sent=true, last_token_seq=842, bytes=73
- gateway: resume.window=1, resume.offset=840->842, response-code=200
- auth-proxy: connection-handoff=client-ephemeral-ipa->edge-ipa, keepalive=reset

Notes: customer captured HAR + service worker console traces and attached them in the ticket (see comments).
steps_to_reproduce: Open electron app with SW enabled
Start SSE stream for long summary
Simulate short network interruption (e.g., throttling) or trigger client timeout
Observe SDK resume and final paragraph missing
investigation_notes: 03-13 18:20 UTC: Replayed customer HAR — saw duplicate CONNECT from client with identical client-id header within 300ms
03-13 19:05 UTC: Reproducer run in staging with a synthetic service-worker replay reproduced missing tail when fetch handler replays the request while SDK issues retry

Hypothesis: service-worker replay path causes browser-level response stream to be intercepted and reconstituted; SDK resume/rewind logic expects monotonic single socket handshake and can drop terminal fragments when two parallel connection sequences race to attach to same session token
Correlation: similar linkage to SUP-314159 (session rotation) where handoff races caused trailing-frame loss
comments: 2026-03-13 18:45 - Customer (BlueWave Support): Attached HAR + SW logs. Noticed that console shows SW replay event immediately before final newline disappears.
2026-03-13 19:10 - Support (Ava Martinez): Acknowledged receipt, escalating to runtime/SRE. Asking for SDK/service-worker repro steps.

2026-03-13 19:40 - SRE (Darren Ng): Reproduced in staging with SW-enabled test harness. Observed both connections claiming resume token; terminal frame emitted by runtime but only consumed by first in-order stream. Second attach path appears to see prefix only.

2026-03-14 08:12 - Runtime Eng (Priya Shah): Added debug logging to resume attach flow and found race in session attach handler where the second attach path nulls the tail buffer after prefix reconciliation. Draft PR created to make attach idempotent.
2026-03-14 09:05 - Support (Ava Martinez): Sent workaround steps (disable SW replay, bump client timeout). Customer applied workaround and confirmed fix for their immediate production impact.
resolution_notes: Workaround accepted by customer: disable service worker fetch-replay for SSE endpoints and increase client socket timeout

Engineering proposed fix: make resume attach idempotent and ensure terminal buffer flush is gated on finalization flag rather than attach order (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/982)
Planned rollout: hotfix to staging channel 2026-03-15, canary to private deployments 2026-03-16, full rollout after 48h monitoring windows
next_steps: Complete runtime PR and add unit/integration tests for dual-attach resume race
Coordinate with SDK team to detect SW replay path and emit a warning in console (SDK PR #173)
Follow up with customer 2026-03-16 to validate hotfix in their private deployment
